verdict.rationale: Hightouch's own docs describe the full warehouse-native loop. Models are defined with SQL, dbt, or table selection on existing warehouse tables. Audiences are built from warehouse data. Syncs activate the data to 300+ destinations without copying it into a separate system. Community comments from the cofounder and users corroborate the SQL-model, no-copy architecture. missing for 10: hands-on independent verification of audience-building on warehouse tables at scale.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can run warehouse-native: define models and audiences on tables already in my warehouse and activate them without re-collecting the data (reverse ETL)

citations.quote: Data teams typically create models by writing SQL in the editor, selecting from tables or views, or re-using dbt models and BI queries from Looker or Sigma.
Hightouch runs on top of your data warehouse, so teams use their existing customer data without copying it into a separate system.
Connect to any data warehouse, lake, or other source. Define the records to sync by selecting a table or writing SQL.
Sync to 300\+ destinations in real-time or on a recurring schedule.
Hightouch's hybrid architecture stores no data in Hightouch itself out of the box—it all stays in the customer's own warehouse/S3 bucket
